{"id": "e9444b9f-df79-4ce4-bc74-f80ecc585892", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Confirmed — AWS already provides a managed policy for this, so you don't need to write your own in most cases.

## Option 1: AWS managed policy (simplest)

Attach **`AmazonDynamoDBReadOnlyAccess`** to your IAM user or role. It grants read-only access to DynamoDB resources across the account via the console and API.

```bash
aws iam attach-role-policy \
  --role-name YourRoleName \
  --policy-arn [redacted ARN]
```

## Option 2: Custom least-privilege policy (scoped to specific tables)

If you want to limit access to one or more specific tables rather than the whole account:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "DynamoDBReadOnly",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "dynamodb:GetItem",
        "dynamodb:BatchGetItem",
        "dynamodb:Query",
        "dynamodb:Scan",
        "dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem",
        "dynamodb:DescribeTable"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:dynamodb:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:table/YourTableName",
        "arn:aws:dynamodb:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:table/YourTableName/index/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Replace `REGION`, `ACCOUNT_ID`, and `YourTableName`. Including `/index/*` covers reads against global/local secondary indexes.
